rules.rule: Hold the S&P 500, except in the 3 calendar months whose VIX was highest (vs its past-year average) in all the years before; T-bills then. Sell at the close before those months start, buy back at the close before they end. 10 bp per switch.

Every Friday close: VIX more than 25% above its normal level for that week of the year → T-bills from the next session; otherwise the S&P 500. Normal = its past-year average × how high the VIX usually was that week in earlier years. 10 bp per switch.
The same, but VIX vs its past-year average only, with no seasonal adjustment: does the seasonality add anything?
